purpose: Teach: 半月/高麗/理学部/無害/音痴/科学技術庁/初等/開発途上国

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、月の半月と新月の比較を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Sakura — you covered the comparison between lunar phases and new moons in your paper, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, encouraging tone with genuine curiosity. Leans in slightly. Steady rhythm, no rush. The cadence of a teacher who remembers what matters to her students.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、古代の高麗王朝研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused my research on ancient Goryeo dynasty studies.
lines.style: Clear and direct, with quiet confidence. No performance. A student answering honestly, not trying to impress. Slight pause before speaking, as if choosing words carefully.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 理学部の応用化学を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Applied chemistry in the science department — that was your focus, wasn't it?
lines.style: Thoughtful, reflective pause before the question. Gentle confirmation rather than accusation. Slow, measured delivery. Voice stays open and curious.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、無害な殺虫成分の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I researched the development of harmless insecticidal compounds.
lines.style: Direct and sincere, without hesitation. Speaks to the substance of the work, not defending it. Calm, grounded tone. A student who believes in what she studied.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 音痴改善の音楽教育を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Music education for improving pitch perception — you wrote about that too?
lines.style: Engaged and present. Light smile in the voice. Acknowledging the breadth of Sakura's interests without judgment. Even pace, genuine follow-up.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、科学技術庁の研究助成史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I examined the history of research grants from the Science and Technology Agency.
lines.style: Steady and straightforward. A student who can pivot between topics without losing composure. No apologetic edge. Matter-of-fact, focused.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 初等教育のデジタル化を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Digitalization in primary education — that was another area you explored, wasn't it?
lines.style: Reflective and measured. Genuine wondering in the voice — not testing, but truly interested in how these threads connect. Slight rise at the end, inviting response.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、開発途上国への医療援助を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I researched healthcare support and development aid programs for developing nations.
lines.style: Clear, committed tone that closes the list. No trailing off. A student stating her work with full conviction. Breath support solid to the final word.
